texts.li: The new plans run straight into {PLACE}. {B_nameDef} would sooner build through it and be done; {A_nameDef} is standing in front of it and says {GOD} was there first. The council is asked to settle where the walls go.

{A_nameDef} came to the council with chalk on {A_possessive} hands: somebody has marked out a wall right over {PLACE}. Move it with the proper words, {A_pronoun} says, or build round it, but nobody tears it down without asking.
[lowtech] The stakes for the new building cross the stones of {PLACE}. {B_nameDef} says stones can be carried. {A_nameDef} says {GOD} cannot.

li.label: Move it, with a rite
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} said the words over {PLACE} that evening, asking {GOD} to bear with being moved, and it was marked to be taken up and set down somewhere better.

li.label: Build round it
li.outcome: The plans were drawn again around {PLACE}, and {B_nameDef} grumbled over the lost room. {A_nameDef} went out to it at dusk to say it would stay where it stood.

li.label: Take it down
li.outcome: The council said the building comes first. {PLACE} is {GOD}'s no longer, and it is to come down. {A_nameDef} went out alone to say goodbye to it, and came back without a word to anyone.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: the feast in a hard season

texts.li: {GOD}'s festival falls tomorrow, and the larder is thin and the walls still scarred. {A_nameDef} asks the council how it is to be kept: as it ought, with less on the table, or with the rite alone, or not at all this year.
{A_nameDef} has been counting what is left in the stores and does not like the sum. Tomorrow is {GOD}'s day, {A_pronoun} says, and the god will be watching what the colony does with it.
[lowtech] The hard days have not ended, and {GOD}'s day is on us at sunrise. {A_nameDef} asks whether there is bread to spare for a feast, or only for a prayer.

li.label: Keep it, with less
li.outcome: The council said {GOD}'s day would be kept, but lean: no offering carried from the stores this year and no guests sent for. {A_nameDef} went to {PLACE} that evening to say so.

li.label: Keep only the rite
li.outcome: No feast this year. The faithful gathered at {PLACE} that evening, and the rite was said in full; tomorrow will be an ordinary working day.

li.label: Let it pass this year
li.outcome: The council let {GOD}'s day go by. {A_nameDef} went to {PLACE} alone at dusk and stayed there longer than anyone thought needful.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} laughed at {GOD} in front of the faithful the other day, loud enough for all to hear. {A_nameDef} wants {B_objective} kept away from {GOD}'s rites for a season; {B_nameDef} says a joke never hurt a god that was really there.

{A_nameDef} has not forgiven {B_nameDef} for the laughing. Let {B_pronoun} stay away from {PLACE}, {A_pronoun} says, or let {B_pronoun} carry the next offering there with {B_possessive} own hands and see how funny it is then.
[lowtech] {B_nameDef} mocked the old ways before {GOD}'s faithful. {A_nameDef} asks the council what a mocker is owed: the door, or the load.

li.label: Keep {B_nameDef} from the rites
li.outcome: The council told {B_nameDef} to keep away from {GOD}'s rites for a season. {A_nameDef} said the words at {PLACE} that evening without {B_objective}, and {B_nameDef} has had a sour face about it since.

li.label: {B_nameDef} carries the next offering
li.outcome: The council set {B_nameDef} to carry {GOD}'s next offering to {PLACE} with {B_possessive} own hands. {B_nameDef} went, rolling {B_possessive} eyes the whole way there, and set it down all the same.

li.label: Let it be
li.outcome: The council would not quarrel over a laugh. {A_nameDef} said nothing more of it, though some say {GOD} was not so ready to forget.

li.why: the council let a scoffer be

texts.li: Nobody left at home keeps {GOD} any more, and {PLACE} stands with dust on it. {A_nameDef} asks the council what is to become of it: kept for the god all the same, given over to another, or left to fall.
The last of {GOD}'s faithful is gone from among us, and {A_nameDef} has noticed that nobody walks out to {PLACE} now. A place of a god left untended sits ill, {A_pronoun} says, one way or the other.
[lowtech] {GOD}'s stones stand with nobody to sweep them. {A_nameDef} asks: tend them still, give them to a god somebody here keeps, or let the weeds have them.

li.label: Keep it for {GOD}
li.outcome: The council said {PLACE} would be kept, faithful or no. {A_nameDef} swept it that evening and said a word there for a god nobody here holds.

li.why: the council kept its place though nobody held it

li.label: Give it to {GOD2}
li.outcome: The council gave {PLACE} to {GOD2}. Someone of {GOD2}'s will walk out and say the words there, and some say {GOD} was not asked.

li.label: Let it fall
li.outcome: The council let {PLACE} go. It is nobody's god's now, and {A_nameDef} walked out to it once more at dusk before leaving it to the weather.
